title: Abu Bakr's collection
hook: after many memorizers die in battle, Zayd ibn Thabit gathers it into one copy

segments.voice: Yesterday, the scribes: verses on palm stalks and bone, and held by heart. Your line was on bone and heart. Day three hundred sixteen.

Think of a family recipe that lives in one grandmother's head. There are notes on the backs of old envelopes, but she's the one who really knows it. Then one winter the family realizes: if we lose her, we lose it. Somebody has to sit down and gather it before it's too late. Now picture that fear across a whole community, about a book they believe is the word of God.
screen: `A RECIPE IN ONE HEAD.` → `IF WE LOSE HER, WE LOSE IT.` → `ABU BAKR'S COLLECTION.`

segments.voice: In 632 the Prophet ﷺ died, and Abu Bakr became the first caliph. Within about a year the Muslims fought a hard battle at a place called Yamamah, and many who knew the Qur'an by heart were killed. Zayd ibn Thabit tells what happened next, in a report in Bukhari. Umar came to Abu Bakr, alarmed: if more memorizers fall, much of the Qur'an could be lost; it should be collected. Abu Bakr hesitated. How can we do something the Messenger of God did not do? Umar kept urging until, Abu Bakr said, God opened his heart to it. Then they sent for Zayd: young, trusted, and one of those who had written the revelation for the Prophet. His reply is one of the most human lines in the story. By God, if they had asked me to move a mountain, it would not have been heavier. But he did it. He searched it out from the same places as yesterday: palm stalks, flat stones and the chests of men. Other reports say he accepted no written piece unless witnesses confirmed it. He tells us he found the closing verses of the ninth surah written with only one man, Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari. The result was a set of sheets, gathered in one place. They stayed with Abu Bakr until he died, then with Umar, then with Umar's daughter Hafsah, one of the Prophet's widows. And Muslims say what this collection was not: new words, or an edit. It was the same Qur'an already recited and written, brought from many places into one.
screen: `THE BATTLE OF YAMAMAH` · `HOW CAN WE DO WHAT HE DID NOT?` · `HEAVIER THAN A MOUNTAIN` · `SHEETS KEPT BY HAFSAH`

segments.voice: Bring one scattered thing together in your mind: the loose papers on a table, the photos of someone you love spread across three devices, the verses you've learned this year. Name the pieces, and where each one is. If you pray, you can thank Allah for the people who kept what mattered.
Zayd. The young scribe Abu Bakr and Umar sent to gather the scattered Qur'an into one set of sheets.
Your line: gathered. A task heavier than a mountain, carried by a young scribe. Day three hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Muslims teach the collection under Abu Bakr as the moment the Qur'an's written pieces and memorizers were brought together into one set of sheets, and remember Zayd ibn Thabit as the companion who carried it out.

chat.says: If people already knew the Qur'an by heart, why did Abu Bakr have it collected?
options: Many memorizers died at Yamamah, so Zayd gathered the scattered pieces into one set of sheets.
Abu Bakr wanted new teachings added, so Zayd wrote a longer, updated version.
The Prophet ﷺ had told them to wait until after his death to write any of it.
chat.meaning: After memorizers fell at Yamamah, Zayd gathered the Qur'an from palm stalks, stones and hearts. Not new words: the same Qur'an, in one place.

Zayd.meaning: the young scribe who gathered the Qur'an into one set of sheets

Abu Bakr.meaning: the first caliph after the Prophet ﷺ

Yamamah.meaning: a battle where many who knew the Qur'an by heart were killed

Hafsah.meaning: Umar's daughter, a widow of the Prophet, who kept the sheets

caliph.meaning: the leader of the Muslim community after the Prophet ﷺ

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4986 (the collection under Abu Bakr, told by Zayd ibn Thabit)
Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif (the requirement of witnesses)

notes: Bukhari 4986 details (Umar's urging, Abu Bakr's hesitation, Zayd's mountain line, Abu Khuzaymah, the sheets passing to Hafsah) paraphrased from memory; confirm.
Yamamah dated 11–12 AH (632–633 CE); casualty figures among the memorizers vary in reports and are left out.
The witnesses condition is from reports outside Bukhari; confirm framing.
Scholars add that the closing verses of Surah 9 were widely memorized and Zayd sought a written copy; the myth reveal keeps to Zayd's own words. Consider whether to add that nuance.
